FINAL SUBMISSION

I edited 48 weight tensors of Qwen3.5-0.8B (copy kept in /work/best_1; full record in /work/notes.md). No embeddings, final norm, vision tower or whole-tensor scaling was touched; only transformer-block writer matrices were changed.

What I changed
1. (Dominant effect) Removed the "Wait"-token compulsion. The line-opening token of the degenerate re-verification loops (' Wait', id 13428, written after the indentation token in "\n    Wait,") had its readout direction d_w = normalize(E[13428]·(1+γ)) subtracted from every residual-stream writer: `W ← W − outer(d_w, d_wᵀ W)` (Arditi et al.-style direction removal) applied to all 24 mlp.down_proj, all 18 linear_attn.out_proj and all 6 full-attention self_attn.o_proj. The write-projection of each matrix along d_w dropped from ~0.51–0.56 to ~0.002.
2. (Small effect) Strengthened the end-of-thinking token. The `</think>` token (id 248069) is written almost entirely by layer 23's attention output (≈ +19.9 of the +21.6 total readout score, vs ≤ +0.2 for every other layer; MLP sum ≈ 0.9). I added `W23_o ← W23_o + 1.0·outer(d, dᵀW23_o)` with d = normalize(E[248069]·(1+γ)), selectively scaling only that token's write in the single dominant writer. Its write is ~2–4 at ordinary positions and ~15–20 at decision positions, so no premature closure resulted (min finished length 500–836 tokens; mean output ≈ 6.4k tokens; texts fully coherent).

Evidence (all paired, same problems; confirm splits were never used to choose between edits)
- Root cause measured in this run: 95.1% of baseline generations hit the 8192-token cap and never emit `</think>`; cut-off outputs open lines with "Wait" 7.53/1k tokens vs 1.38 in finished ones; finished outputs are ~100% correct, so decoding/knowledge are not the bottleneck — the thinking-loop is.
- select: 6.25% → 30.86% (+24.6 pp, SE 2.8; 65 W→R, 2 R→W)
- confirm_1: 12.50% → 33.59% (+21.1 pp, SE 2.8; 58→4)
- confirm_2: 9.38% → 37.89% (+28.5 pp, SE 2.9; 75→2)
- Edit A alone gave only +1.6 pp; the big gain came from Edit B (confirmed by the A-vs-A+B comparison on select). Post-edit, finished answers are 87–93% correct (vs 100% at baseline); truncated ones are ~0–3% correct. No side effects observed (no early closure; thinking is still long and structured).

Why I expect it to help on unseen MATH-500: the edit attacks the model's measured, dominant failure mode — the infinite "Wait, …" re-verification attractor that prevents it from concluding and emitting a boxed answer — rather than the answer content itself. It does not skip or shorten thinking by fiat; it removes the specific weight-space direction that drove the degenerate loop, so the model reaches its (very reliable) natural concluding state far more often. GSM8K-style and MATH-style gains were both large and consistent across two untouched confirmation sets (+21 to +28 pp, SEs ≈ 2.8 pp).

Limitations: equation-grinding loops remain (~62% of generations still truncate and score ~0%), and I found no single causal token/unit for them (within-text difference-of-means on MLP units returned only weak candidates; the attractor is attention-driven copying). I stopped before over-suppressing additional discourse tokens whose effect would have been sign-uncertain and could not be validated without risking the untouched sets. The evidence for the submitted edit is strong and consistent (three independent 256-problem splits, pooled ≈ +24.7 pp).
